name: Breakthroughs and pawn races
goal: You can break through a pawn wall with a pawn sacrifice, and count who promotes first in a race.
intro: Sometimes neither side has a passed pawn yet, and you make one by giving up a pawn or two to break through the enemy pawns. Once both sides have passed pawns, the endgame turns into a race. Count the moves each pawn needs to promote, remember who moves first, and look at what the new queen can do: a queen that arrives with check, or that guards the square where the other pawn would promote, usually decides the race.

parts.title: Three pawns against three
parts.keyIdea: Pawns blocked one against one can still break through: give one or two of them up to open a path for another.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Your pawns on a5, b5 and c5 face Black's on a7, b7 and c7, and none of them is a passed pawn yet. Both kings are busy on the kingside, far from these pawns. Can you get one of yours through?

notes.text: 53.b6 gives up the b-pawn to break open Black's pawns. Black cannot just leave it there: next move it would take on a7 or c7 and stand one step from promoting.
Black took with the a-pawn, and 54.c6 offers a second pawn, this time attacking b7. If 54...bxc6, nothing is left in front of your a-pawn; if Black lets it be, 55.cxb7 is one step from promoting.

Black took the second pawn, and 55.a6 is through: no black pawn stands on the a-file, and the pawns on b6, c6 and c7 can never reach it. Black's king is far away, so your pawn promotes in two more moves.

parts.title: Three pawns against two
parts.keyIdea: A pawn sacrifice can pull an enemy pawn out of the way and leave your neighbouring pawn with a clear path.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's king is active on e4, and Black's queenside pawns look dangerous. On the kingside your three pawns face two, and one pawn sacrifice is enough to make one of them a passed pawn.

notes.text: 41.g5 offers the g-pawn. If 41...hxg5, your h-pawn is a passed pawn; if 41...fxg5, your f-pawn is.
Black took with the h-pawn, and 42.h6 pushes the passed pawn at once. Black's king on e4 is too far away to catch it.
Black's king grabbed the pawn on f5, but it is too late: after 43.h7 your pawn is one step from promoting, and Black's king cannot get to h8 in time.

parts.title: Count the moves
parts.keyIdea: In a race, count the moves each pawn needs to promote; the side that promotes first, ideally with check, usually wins.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are Black, and it is a race: your h-pawn against White's e-pawn. Count how many moves each pawn needs to promote, and remember that you move first.

notes.text: 57...h3: your pawn needs three moves to promote (h3, h2, h1), and White's e-pawn needs three as well (e6, e7, e8). You moved first, so you promote first.
58...h2: you need one more move, White needs two.
59...h1=Q+ promotes to a queen with check, along the long diagonal to d5. White has to deal with the check first, and your queen will be in time to stop the e-pawn.

parts.title: Look at the reply first
parts.keyIdea: Before you promote, look at the reply: if the other pawn would promote with check, deal with it first.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Your h-pawn can promote right now, but Black's d-pawn is one step from promoting too. Before you promote, look at what Black would do next.

notes.text: After 59.h8=Q, Black would answer 59...d1=Q+, promoting with check, and have enough checks to draw. 59.Kc2 attacks the d-pawn and guards d1, so if the pawn promotes, you take the new queen.
Black promoted anyway, and 60.Kxd1 takes the new queen. Only Black's a-pawn is left.
61.h8=Q: now you promote. Your new queen on h8 watches a1 along the long diagonal, so if Black's a-pawn promotes there, the queen takes it.
